title: Dr Ambedkar and the working class
author: Editorial Desk
summary: Ahead of Ambedkar Jayanti on 14 April, a look at his work on labour.
body:
**Dr Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar** (1891–1956) is remembered as the chief architect of the Constitution. He was also a thinker and a policy-maker on labour.

## Labour Member

From 1942 to 1946 he served as **Labour Member** in the Viceroy's Executive Council. In that period the Government took up questions such as working hours, employment exchanges, workers' insurance and the tripartite labour conference.

## The Independent Labour Party

In 1936 he founded the **Independent Labour Party**, which focused on the problems of the landless, tenants and industrial workers.

## Constitutional work

Several labour-related provisions found their way into the Directive Principles. His final speech to the Constituent Assembly warned that political democracy could not last without social and economic democracy.

## Thengadi Ji and Ambedkar

BMS's account of Thengadi Ji's life records that he was close to Ambedkar in his last years, formed the **Samajik Samarasata Manch** on Ambedkar Jayanti in 1983, and wrote a book about him.

## The common thread

Both argued that the dignity of labour is inseparable from social equality. For any union, that is not a theory but a daily test.
